Appearance:
 Shri Siddharth Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Ravindra Dixit - Government Advocate for the respon
ORDER Both the parties are heard.

2. Petitioner has preferred this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India being aggrieved by impugned order dated 5.9.2024 (Annexure P/1), whereby the petitioner has been transferred from Municipal Council Kailaras, Morena to Municipal Council, Madhusudangarh,
District Guna.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was working as Assistant Revenue Inspector, Municipal Council, Kailaras, District Morena and one enquiry was initiated by the respondents against the petitioner alleging that certain financial irregularities have been committed by the petitioner and other officers of the Municipal Council Kailaras, Morena.
Against initiation of the enquiry, another employee preferred Writ Petition No.29325/2022 before this Court and this Court has passed the interim order dated 3.4.2023 (Annexure P/3).
Despite the interim order passed by the Court, respondents got registered an FIR against the petitioner and other employees.

On the basis of FIR, respondents have transferred the petitioner but the Chief Municipal Officer who is administrative NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15725 2 WP-27167-2024 head of Municipal Council has not been transferred and posted at Guna itself.
The respondents are acting at the behest of political authority and there is no basis for initiating an enquiry against the petitioner.

sentences.text: The transfer order is ex facie illegal and against the Policy of the Government, therefore, the petitioner preferred the instant writ petition.

4 . Per contra , counsel for the respondents/State opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by submitting that the petitioner is facing enquiry as well as criminal prosecution under Sections 409,
420, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC and under Sections 7, 13(1)(a), 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act,
1988.

As per transfer policy issued by the General Administration Department, Government of M.P.,
petitioner does not deserve for any relief.

5. From perusal of the FIR (Annexure P/4), it appears that the offence under Sections 409, 420,
468, 471, 120-B of IPC and under Sections 7, 13(1)(a), 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 has been registered against the petitioner and some other employees and it has been prima facie found that the petitioner along with other employees on the basis of forged document, paid the amount of Rs.1,41,75,825/- and committed financial irregularities.

In the impugned order dated 5.9.2024 (Annexure P/1), it has been mentioned that as per clause 94 of Circular No.F6-1/2021/Ek/9 dated 24.6.2021, if Lokayukt Organization/Economic Offence Wing or police registered a criminal case against a Government servant and proceeding of prosecution has been started, then there is a possibility to influence the enquiry, therefore, such employee should be transferred.
Petitioner is facing the aforesaid enquiry, therefore, has been transferred by the impugned order.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that Chief Municipal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:15725 3 WP-27167-2024 Officer who is the Administrative Head of the Municipal Council has not been transferred and he remain posted at Morena itself, therefore, the act of the respondents are arbitrary and they are acting beyond jurisdiction.

sentences.text: 7. This Court is not considering the case of concerning Municipal Officer.
At this stage, this Court cannot make any enquiry or marshaling about the criminal liabilities of the petitioner and other accused persons.
Therefore, aforesaid contention made by the petitioner is not accepted.
8. Apart from above, transfer is an incident of service.
No one much less petitioner has any vested right to be posted at a particular place of posting.

It is well settled in law that employer is the best judge to organize its work force and it is also well settled in law that a transfer order cannot be subjected to judicial review unless and until same is found to be influenced by mala fide or arbitrary exercise of powers which petitioner fails to do so.
Concept of equality as enshrined under Article 14 and 16 of Constitution of India, has no application to the cases of transfers 9.

The Division Bench of this court in the matter of Kushal Singh Dodve Vs. Santram Chouhan and others passed in WA No. 234/2015 vide order dated 30/6/2015 has held that:
"9.

The scope of judicial review is very limited and this Court would not interfere with the order of transfer lightly, because the Courts do not substitute their own decision in the matter of transfer and if we allow to continue the impugned order, the same may cause prejudice to the administrative functioning of the Municipal Council,

sentences.text: The writ petition is still pending.
No reply has been filed by the State and Municipal Council, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15725 4 WP-27167-2024 Barwani.

10. It is well settled that even if a transfer order is passed in violation of executive instructions or orders, the Court ordinarily should not interfere with the order, instead affected party should approach the higher authorities in the department.

If the Courts continue to interfere with day-to-day transfer orders issued by the Government and its subordinate authorities, there will be complete chaos in administration, which would not be conductive to public interest."

10. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the judgment passed by the Division Bench in the case of Kushal Singh Dodve (Supra) , no interference is required in the impugned transfer order.
Impugned order has rightly been passed and same does not call for any interference in the present petition.
11. Petition sans merit and is hereby dismissed.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE (alok)
